title: 2D Gamma divergence: split the integrand into v(q) and the chi/F subtraction — the residual 1/N gap drift sits in the integral of F(q)
symptom: The Coulomb-derived GW gap drifts as 1/N with the q mesh ('整个库伦计算得到的gap是1/N收敛'). The earlier explanation that attributed this to the mesh average of the bare leading eigenvalue lambda_1(q) was withdrawn as the wrong diagnostic.
root_cause: The level energy is assembled as sum_{q != 0} [M(k-q) v(q) - M(k) F(q)] + M(q) * integral F(q) (compensation-function splitting of the q -> 0 singularity). With a correct compensation function the discrete q-sum converges quickly, and what is left unhandled when the singularity is not subtracted exactly is the integral of F(q). In the auxiliary-basis representation the divergence structure is angular-momentum dependent — 1/q^2 between two nodeless s-type NAOs and 1/q between a nodeless s-type and any other NAO — so a 2D compensation function must reproduce the 2D 1/q behaviour (not the 3D 1/q^2), and may need two terms (F1 + F2).
minimal_fix: Instrument the two pieces separately — the discrete q-sum of [M(k-q)v(q) - M(k)F(q)] and the analytic term M(k)*integral F(q) — identify which of them carries the 1/N drift, and fix the compensation function so the correct power of q is subtracted exactly at q -> 0 for the 2D kernel.
validation: Show that the v(q) piece is already converged with the q mesh while the F(q) integral carries the residual drift, then verify the gap is mesh-independent (Gamma-centred vs shifted meshes, two mesh densities) once the correct F is used.
avoid: Do not use the mesh average of the bare leading eigenvalue lambda_1(q) as the convergence diagnostic (explicitly withdrawn as the wrong criterion), and do not apply a 3D 1/q^2 compensation function to the 2D kernel.
